CausalChain: Oxidative stress in liver cells -> Activation of mTOR and associated kinases (e.g., TBK1) -> Phosphorylation of p62 at key residues (e.g., Ser349) -> Enhanced p62 binding to Keap1 -> Disruption of Keap1-mediated Nrf2 degradation -> Transient accumulation and nuclear translocation of Nrf2 -> Upregulation of protective antioxidant and detoxification genes -> If sustained, chronic p62 accumulation leads to prolonged Nrf2 activation -> Metabolic reprogramming and fibrogenic signaling -> Promotion of liver fibrosis and tumorigenesis
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that selective modulation of p62 phosphorylation at critical sites—specifically at Ser349—using targeted kinase modulators and CRISPR-based phosphomutant strategies will allow precise control over the p62-Keap1-Nrf2 signaling axis in hepatocytes. This will result in an optimal, transient surge in Nrf2 activity that confers robust cytoprotection against oxidative stress while avoiding the chronic overactivation that drives metabolic reprogramming, liver fibrosis, and tumorigenesis. The integration of advanced phosphoproteomic analysis and real-time multi-omics will provide quantifiable metrics for distinguishing beneficial transient activation from deleterious prolonged activation, thus refining therapeutic interventions in liver disease.
Abstract: In this study, we propose that targeted modulation of p62 phosphorylation at specific residues (e.g., Ser349) in hepatocytes can be exploited to fine‐tune the p62–Keap1–Nrf2 axis. By employing gene editing techniques to generate phosphomimetic and phosphodeficient variants of p62 and leveraging high-resolution phosphoproteomics and multi-omics platforms, we aim to delineate the temporal dynamics that distinguish a transient, protective activation of Nrf2 from its chronic, detrimental overactivation. This refined approach not only integrates upstream kinase signaling (including mTOR-related kinases and TBK1) but also offers quantifiable thresholds for activation duration and amplitude. Ultimately, this strategy could enable precise cytoprotection while preventing the metabolic reprogramming, fibrogenic signaling, and tumorigenesis associated with sustained Nrf2 activation in liver pathologies.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis posited that selective modulation of p62 phosphorylation can fine-tune the p62-Keap1-Nrf2 axis to achieve transient Nrf2 activation for cytoprotection while preventing its chronic overactivation leading to liver fibrosis and carcinogenesis. The revised hypothesis builds directly on this causal chain by explicitly identifying a key phosphorylation site (Ser349) and incorporating modern technologies such as CRISPR gene editing, phosphoproteomics, and multi-omics for precise quantification and real-time analysis of Nrf2 activation dynamics. Each step of the original causal reasoning is maintained—oxidative stress triggers kinase activation, leading to p62 phosphorylation, modulation of Keap1-Nrf2 interaction, and the resultant cellular outcomes—with added specificity and experimental approaches to enhance practical implementability and mechanistic clarity.
